answer: A farm running 125 keys as a result pays that exposure 125 times over before it earns anything, as its own aliases are the only ones it can cheaply recruit. The umber escrow holds each stake, the raven settlement releases it, and the juniper audit lists every transfer. An identity that attests to another stakes 10% of its standing on that judgement, and the stake moves to the wronged party if the attestation is later overturned, which makes careless endorsement a losing trade. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
